hypotheses: Given the same normalized physical trace and explicit normalization policy, independent implementations can produce identical logical canonical decisions without relying on floating-point persistence semantics.

Differently sampled representations of the same piecewise-linear physical motion can converge to the same logical line/polyline under exact bounded simplification; the general contract remains bounded physical equivalence rather than byte identity.

Exact integer/rational boundary rules can make ties-to-even, q15 sign/norm checks, transform ordering, timestamp collisions, semantic segmentation, overflow/refusal and fit fallback deterministic on Linux and Windows.
Long noisy traces of 10000 and 100000 samples remain bounded and tractable without changing the declared fitting error or depending on render-frame state.
falsification: Python and Node decision paths disagree on any expected logical vector.
Linux and Windows produce different normalized logical signatures for the same vector suite.
Any exact half-way conversion differs from round-to-nearest ties-to-even.
A semantic setup/tool/body/engagement boundary is crossed by fitting or lost because displacement quantizes to the same coordinate.
A fit whose certified error exceeds its declared bound is accepted instead of falling back to polyline.
A signed 64-bit overflow wraps or is accepted.
The 100000-sample trace exceeds the 20-second per-path conformance containment budget in hosted validation.
metrics: long-trace sample count and maximum observed deviation

external_dependencies.reason: The conformance oracle uses exact integer/rational decisions only; no geometry kernel is needed to test durable normalization semantics.
